cases.name: Sara Marie Frye
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Sara brought an undeniable energy into the lives of those who had the pleasure of knowing her. She was embodiment kindness and friendliness, never meeting a stranger and always ready to lend a helping hand.

At the core of Sara’s life were her children. She treasured her role as a mother and delighted in the joy of playing with them, filling their lives with warmth and creativity. Her proudest accomplishments included earning her CNA and later her LPN, milestones reflective of her strong dedication to helping others. She worked diligently in various manufacturing positions throughout her career, but it was her compassionate spirit that truly defined her professional path.

Sara's journey through education began at King’s Gate Elementary, where her foundations were laid before she graduated from Bethel Acres High School. Her determination led her to Gordon Cooper, where she achieved her CNA and LPN certifications, stepping boldly into a world where she could make a difference.

Sara was a woman of many interests and talents. She took great pleasure in expressing herself creatively and was always up for a good laugh. Friends and family describe her as a fun-loving person who could light up any room with her presence. The memories made with her will forever be cherished, as she had an unparalleled ability to bring joy to those around her.

Family meant everything to Sara."
cases.narrative: He allegedly shot her in the face with a shotgun, then claimed she committed suicide. He then filled the wound on her face with petroleum jelly.
